title: Analytics permissions mapper for tenant-aware endpoint and usage views
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Summary:
Implement a centralized 'permissions mapper' layer that enforces tenant-aware RBAC for analytics API endpoints and the Console usage views. The mapper will translate entitlement records (datasets, metrics, dashboards) and role grants into query scoping rules, column-level visibility masks, and response filters so views and endpoints only return authorized data.

Context and motivation:
Console usage dashboards and ad-hoc analytics endpoints currently rely on a mix of client-side filtering and per-endpoint checks. We have observed two problems: (1) inconsistent enforcement across endpoints leading to audit gaps, and (2) duplicate permission logic causing performance regressions and maintenance overhead. This ticket builds a single backend component that is authoritative for analytics permission decisions and can be reused by the API gateway, analytics service, and pre-aggregation jobs.

Goals:
- Provide deterministic tenant-aware query scoping for all analytics endpoints (grouped by dataset/dashboards/metric).
- Support column-level masking for PII and restricted fields based on grant type.
- Expose a low-latency permission evaluation cache that respects realtime entitlement updates (invalidate via entitlement-syncer events).
- Emit audit events for decisioning (allow/deny) and reason codes for downstream observability.
- Keep per-request overhead < 3ms on p95 in common cases (cached decisions).

Out of scope:
- UI-level role management UX (product will own).
- Full policy language; we will support a conservative rule set covering dataset grants, role-to-tenant mapping, and column masks.
acceptance_criteria: Permissions mapper deployed behind analytics API and used for /usage and /queries endpoints
Service returns data filtered by dataset-level grants; denied requests receive HTTP 403 with audit_reason
Column-level masking applied when grant excludes sensitive fields; masked fields replaced with null or '<redacted>' per policy
Decision cache invalidates within 30s after entitlement-syncer publishes update (configurable TTL), verified by integration test
Audit events (decision, principal, resource, reason) emitted to analytics-audit topic and visible in Console debug trace
tasks: Design data model for permission records and mask rules (schema in Confluence)
Implement permission lookup API and local decision cache in analytics-service
Add middleware to enforce query scoping for SQL/DSL pipelines and pre-aggregation jobs
Hook entitlement-syncer event listener to invalidate cache entries
Add audit event emission and wire to existing audit pipeline
Write integration tests simulating multi-tenant grants and revocations
Performance test with synthetic traffic to measure p95 decision latency
notes: Design decision: keep rules simple and deterministic rather than adopting a full RBAC policy language. This reduces evaluation cost and limits surprising allow/deny behaviors.

Trade-off: column-level masking is implemented at the service layer (post-query) initially to avoid reworking multiple query engines. Longer-term optimization could push masking into the query planner for predicates and storage savings.
Cache strategy: negative/deny results are cached for 10s to avoid noisy revocation race conditions; allow decisions cached for 5m with eviction on entitlement change events.
Performance mitigation: use prefix-keyed cache and compacted permission fingerprints to make lookups O(1). If p95 > 3ms, offload evaluation to a small in-cluster sidecar store for hot principals.
Audit: decisions should include a stable reason code (e.g., DATASET_NO_ACCESS, COLUMN_MASKED, ORG_SUSPENDED) for downstream alerting and QA.

Fallback: if permission service is unreachable, endpoints will follow conservative-deny policy for high-sensitivity requests and a configurable degraded-allow for low-sensitivity metrics with warning logs. This behavior must be gated by a runtime flag for controlled rollout.
